relationships.rationale: Twelve-factor patterns are the concrete baseline that makes an application cloud-native by design.
Cloud-native operability — horizontal scaling, immutable deploys, routine restarts — depends on application processes holding no durable state.
A cloud-native operating model is built on environments described as code and deploys that replace immutable artefacts rather than mutating servers.
Assembling commodity capability rather than building it depends on those capabilities being composable, replaceable services rather than embedded in a monolith.
This strategy is the direct mandate for composing capabilities from independent, replaceable services with monoliths as the exception.
Independently replaceable services are only independent in practice if each can be deployed without coordinating with other teams.
Deploying on demand via automated pipelines depends on each service being independently deployable without cross-team coordination.
Continuous delivery pipelines are where dependency scanning and policy checks run, shifting security into the development workflow rather than a release gate.
On-demand automated deployment depends on environments and artefacts being defined as code and deployed immutably.
This strategy is the direct mandate for every service exposing health, structured logs, metrics, and traces from day one.
Each service selecting its own primary data store for fit depends on services holding no shared durable state, with state externalised to the store that fits the workload.
